great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: “Unlimited Automatic Recharge... re-instatement of up to the base Sum Insured unlimited times in a policy year... Recharge amount can be utilized for same illness as well as different Illnesses.”
great.explanation: Automatically reinstates up to the base Sum Insured unlimited times in a policy year, and it can be used for the same or different illnesses. This can significantly increase available cover in a year with multiple or recurring hospitalizations.

great.name: Built-in SI Buffer
great.quote: “The Company agrees to automatically make the re-instatement of up to the base Sum Insured unlimited times in a policy year... utilized only after the base Sum Insured has been completely exhausted”
great.explanation: Provides an automatic additional cover up to the base Sum Insured (unlimited times) once the base Sum Insured is fully exhausted. This protects you from running out of cover mid-year after large claims.

great.name: NCB
great.quote: “At the end of each Policy Year, the Company will enhance the Sum Insured by 10% flat... (vi) In the event of a Claim there is no impact on the accrual of Cumulative Bonus.”
great.explanation: Sum Insured increases by 10% each policy year and a claim does not impact the accrual of this cumulative bonus. This is valuable because your bonus growth continues even in years when you use the policy.

great.name: ICU Charges
great.quote: “The eligible ICU Charges applicable for the Insured Person under the Policy is 'No limit'”
great.explanation: ICU charges have 'No limit' under the policy. This reduces the risk of ICU bills being capped separately, subject to the overall Sum Insured.

great.name: Co-pay
great.explanation: Only a definition of co-payment is provided and no applied co-pay clause is stated. No co-pay is charged on this plan — the insurer bears 100% of all admissible claims, which is better than policies that charge 10–20% co-pay.

good.name: Room Rent
good.quote: “The eligible Room Rent or Room Category applicable for the Insured Person under the Policy is 'Single Private AC room'.”
good.explanation: Hospital room eligibility is limited to a 'Single Private AC room'. This is a standard room entitlement and helps avoid room-category related deductions if you stay within this category.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED)... shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage...”
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are not covered for the first 36 months of continuous coverage. Claims for declared/undeclared PEDs will be payable only after this waiting period is completed.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: “Named Ailment Waiting Period... shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage...”
good.explanation: Named ailments are excluded for the first 24 months of continuous coverage. You should expect claims for those listed conditions to be payable only after 2 years.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: “30-day waiting period... Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident...”
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are not covered in the first 30 days from the first policy start date, except for accidents. This is the standard initial waiting period in retail health insurance.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: “For a period of 60 days immediately prior to the Insured Person's date of admission to the Hospital...”
good.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses for up to 60 days immediately before hospitalization. This helps pay for consultations, tests, and medicines leading up to admission.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: “For a period of 90 days immediately after the Insured Person's date of discharge from the hospital...”
good.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses for up to 90 days immediately after discharge. This supports follow-up treatment costs like medicines, diagnostics, and doctor visits.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: “Any item or condition or treatment specified in List of Non-Medical Items (Annexure – I to Policy Terms & Conditions).”
bad.reference: Clause 4.2 (1) Specific Exclusions + Annexure I (List of Expenses Generally Excluded)
bad.explanation: Items listed as non-medical/consumables in Annexure I are excluded from cover. This can increase out-of-pocket costs during hospitalization for items like gloves, masks, and procedure kits.

unclear.name: Cashless Network
unclear.quote: “Network Provider... means the Hospitals enlisted by an Insurer, TPA... to provide medical services... by a Cashless Facility.”
unclear.explanation: Cashless treatment is available at hospitals enlisted as 'Network Providers'. The document does not state the number or list of network hospitals, so the practical reach of cashless access cannot be assessed from this extract.
